title: Ligand-constrained assembly of a quartz-topology metal–organic framework for the uptake of emerging contaminants and trace-level water monitoring
content: The development of advanced porous materials for the removal and monitoring of emerging contaminants remains a key challenge in environmental chemistry. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of MUDEC-4(Zn), a new metal–organic framework constructed from a pyrazolone-derived ligand (H2L = (E)-N′-((1-butyl-5-hydroxy-3-methyl-1H-pyrazol-4-yl)(phenyl)methylene)isonicotinohydrazide; [Zn(L)]n). Despite the well-known coordination versatility of pyrazolone compounds, their use as building blocks in MOF chemistry has remained scarcely explored. The designed ligand imposes geometric constraints on the coordination environment, stabilizing a three-dimensional framework with a rare quartz-like (qtz) topology composed of distorted tetrahedrally connected Zn nodes and chiral helicoidal channels. The structure was determined by three-dimensional electron diffraction and complementary spectroscopic techniques. MUDEC-4(Zn) exhibits high chemical and thermal stability together with accessible microporosity (SBET = 836.5 m2 g−1 and micropore volume of 0.277 cm3 g−1). The material is able to remove more than 80% of propylparaben at 0.5 mg L−1 concentration within 10 min, and has a maximum adsorption capacity of 170 mg g−1. The pore walls, lined by the hydrophobic butyl and phenyl substituents of the ligand, provide the necessary anchoring sites that drive the adsorption of parabens and benzophenones (as key emerging contaminants), rationalizing the high adsorption capacity (Qmax = 170 mg g−1, Langmuir model) and the trace-level sensitivity of the combined MUDEC-4(Zn)-µ-dSPE-UHPLC-MS/MS method (estimated LODs in the 3.7 to 20 ng L−1 range). These results establish pyrazolone-isonicotinoylhydrazone frameworks as a rationally designed platform for environmental analytical applications.
